- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility clustering.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — apply lagged correction or dampen momentum after peak.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to recognize it — reduce forecast slope or add decay factor.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign horizon — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment swing duration or use sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term volatility spikes — consider sentiment-driven volatility scaling or adaptive horizon adjustment.
